task: Write the design note for W2-68 (DAEO-2gc7), `docs/research/W2-68-batched-close.md`, from the lead's draft, checked against the code on `w2/integrate` and the sources (batch 0: the note only, no code, no tests).
status: PACKAGES — the note is written and committed (222 lines). Every decision in the draft is kept, nine statements about existing code are corrected, and four open points come back as decision packages.
work_completed: I compared the draft with `select.py`, `evidence.py`, `nightly.py`, `command.py` (CLI, pre-close gate, `_check_governance`, `_scope`, `_run_tests`), `repo.py`, `store/loader.py` and `store/__init__.py`, `rebuild/command.py` and `rebuild/check.py`, `retrieval/lexical.py` and `semantic.py`, `test-map.yaml` and its schema, the ticket file, the W2-68 card (WBS §2), and DEC-880, DEC-883, DEC-884, DEC-889 items 1–3, DEC-890 and DEC-899. W1-30's named case was read by name and body; it is outside this ticket's acceptance folder. The note keeps the lead's sections 0 to 10 in their order: the two fingerprints and what they leave out, the path map and test map counted as code, "cannot be computed" read as fresh, the batch's seven steps, the seven reuse conditions, the red batch's attribution, the store row and checks, the tables of what is recorded where and what each step reads, the failure KPIs and where each is refused, the allowed paths, the residuals, and section 10 left for the trial's figures. I added section 11 (the packages) and ended with section 12, "Corrections to the lead's draft".
files_changed: docs/research/W2-68-batched-close.md
evidence: Commit `f8bc5203`, "W2-68: the design note, before any code (DEC-883, DEC-889, DEC-890)", trailers `Task: DAEO-2gc7`, `Role: engineer`, `Implements: DEC-883, DEC-889, DEC-890`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; 1 file, 222 insertions. `git log --oneline -2` shows f8bc5203 then 966b9f6b. `git status --short` shows only untracked placeholder device files (`.bashrc`, `.gitmodules`, `.idea` and others, `crw-rw-rw- nobody 1,3`), which the sandbox put there; none are mine and none were touched. Step 0: (a) failed as required (`OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, exit 1); (b) worked (`hash-object` exit 0, `update-index --refresh` exit 0). `gov.__file__` line: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-68/src/gov/__init__.py`. Before committing, `/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.git/hooks` held no `pre-commit`, only samples. `w2/integrate` and HEAD were both `966b9f6b` when the code was read. `gov retrieve`: tried once, for how a close picks its green base; it answered `STORE_MISSING` because this worktree has no store. I did not rebuild one, since that would write `.gov-runtime/store.db` outside scratch, so I read the named files directly. Read refusals: 0. Scratch: I created no scratch files (0 inodes, 0 bytes); the only folder under `.gov-runtime/scratch/` is the lead's.
tests: none run (none asked for in batch 0)
discoveries: (1) The recovery-rebuild check (CAP-38.b, `gov.rebuild.check`, run by `gov check`) compares the store's digest with a clean load. A `fingerprints` table that counted toward `_digest` would turn it red after every `refresh` (package C). (2) The close's and the nightly's JUnit XML live under `.gov-runtime/` and are not committed, so reuse works only on the machine that ran the run; anywhere else the close safely runs fresh (now a residual in the note). (3) W2-66's `select._form` ignores only acceptance suites, so a reused run of the record-reading set must also ignore `tests/unit` and the other folders under `tests/`. (4) The pre-close gate's `gov check` runs before `_scope`, so reuse has to be decided before that gate. (5) The lexical and semantic `refresh` functions are already incremental, so no file under `src/gov/retrieval/` needs to change. (6) W1-30's `test_a_store_rebuilt_without_embeddings_is_stale_one_commit_later` still holds under the design, because the row's head stops being HEAD after any later commit. (7) Nights state skips only as `tests_run.skipped`, with no `skip_count` (package D).
risks: Reuse condition 4 requires at least one case in every JUnit file named. A legitimate run that wrote a file with no case would make that run not reusable; this is safe (a fresh run) but costs time. Reusing the batch's `gov check` for closes at H plus record-only commits departs from `_check_governance`'s rule that it stands only on a result of the commit being closed (package A).
lessons: In a launched session `gov retrieve` cannot run here until a store exists, and an engineer may not build one, so read the named files directly. `git status` shows sandbox placeholder device files as untracked; commit by path only.
proposed_decisions: A — the batch's `gov check` serves closes whose records differ from H. Options: (a) keep one check per batch as DEC-883 item 1 a says, with the gap named as a residual; (b) reuse the check only when the records fingerprint is equal; (c) every close runs its own (about 7 min a ticket). Recommend (a), confidence medium. B — which schema judges a past commit's test map. Recommend the commit's own `template/governance/kernel/schemas/test-map.schema.json` (then `governance/kernel/schemas/`), else the running package's; confidence medium-high. C — keep the `fingerprints` table out of the store's `_digest` and `_TABLES`, and require that an incremental load of a commit gives the same digest as a full load of it, so the CAP-38.b check stays green; confidence high. D — reuse condition 5 reads a night's `tests_run.skipped` as its stated skip count; a batch's record states `skip_count` itself; confidence high.
unresolved: Packages A to D await the lead's or the owner's decision. Section 10 (the trial's figures) waits for implementation.
recommended_next_action: Decide packages A to D and fold them into the note, then give the note to the test designer before any code.
